key_insight: Differential Spectral Damping (DSD) regularization adapts penalty strength to local eigengap reliability, preserving trustworthy eigen-directions while suppressing unstable ones in ill-conditioned kernel systems.
engineering_relevance: For kernel-based models such as LSTSVM, DSD offers a principled alternative to uniform Tikhonov damping when spectral decay makes matrix inversion numerically fragile.
method: Uses Davis-Kahan sin(Θ) perturbation theory to identify reliable vs. corrupted eigenvectors
Applies differential damping based on local spectral gaps rather than a single global regularization weight
Selects an exponential damping form for smoothness, differentiability, and saturation behavior
evidence_signal: Across real-world benchmarks, DSD improved LSTSVM accuracy by +4.8 points on GINA, +10.4 points at d=200, and +2.6 points on Madelon; pre-image recovery matched Tikhonov at high noise and both reduced naive inversion error by 66×.
watch_item: Benefits appear strongest in highly ill-conditioned regimes (roughly d ≥ 100 and condition number > 10^3), and DSD can underperform simpler regularizers in lower-noise or less severe settings.
paper_title: Differential Spectral Damping Gap Adaptive Regularization for Ill-Conditioned Kernel Methods
